files.rationale: Most claims are carried, many in reduced form, by the promoted legacy transition, legacy payload, route descriptor, spec, vision and compatibility harness docs; six claims (split-transaction rule, bin.fgos removal, metadata split, hash/pretty tests, differential corpus, host-first cost) have no carrier.

claims.rationale: Document title is carried as the title of the promoted architecture document.

Source states "vision/architecture advisory, not a locked law, not an implementation plan", date 2026-09-10 and a revision pointer to an architecture review; target metadata only says Design status Draft / Canonical after review and drops the date and the review pointer.

Target carries that the legacy lane bypasses the kernel and that the kernel has one boundary (invocation-kernel.md section 1), but not the read-first dependency, the "scaffolding that disappears once Node migration completes" framing, or the "never reaches Router or InvocationService" wording beyond "bypasses the kernel".

Navigation header of the legacy source ("Migration Status Note"); the source itself says the document is a legacy-current source during the 2026-09-14 promotion pass, so it only has meaning while the source exists. The target carries its own Source type and Related Files table.

Time-bound note pointing from the legacy source to the four promoted docs and the ledger; the targets link back to the source in their Related Files tables, so the navigation is superseded by the promoted docs themselves.
Section "1. Two Distinct Adapters" is merged into the target "1. Claim" section (two distinct adapters).
Target preserved rule: captured stdout/stderr remain public presentation, not semantic ProviderOutcome; same point as the false-impression warning.

Target says only that LegacyCliPassthroughProvider is CLI-only and bypasses the kernel. Missing: preserved OsString argv, inherited stdin, cwd/env/signal context, returns bytes plus exit/signal, never returns ProviderOutcome, never reachable from remote/chat hosts, descriptor lookup, direct exec of the Node payload, one invocation record through the shared recorder (spec.md section 5 carries only OsString and no-InvocationService).

Target states LegacySemanticProvider is a normal semantic provider introduced per operation when a non-CLI host needs Node behavior. Missing: real versioned contracts OperationRequest/ProviderOutcome, Node bridge calls an extracted use case never bin/fgos.mjs nor an envelope parser, and the admit-select-grant-invoke-normalize-record pipeline participation.
Target keeps "captured stdout/stderr remain public presentation". Missing: supervised child improves CLI cancellation and tracing, and the rule that it never becomes the bridge used by a remote host.

Both adapters delegate a complete use case and a host must not split one state transaction between native and legacy providers unless a component contract defines locking, atomicity, recovery, authority. Target node-to-rust-migration says migrate complete use-case boundaries, but that is about migration order, not an adapter rule against split transactions; no target states the split-transaction prohibition.

Target carries "payload resolved from active release manifest, not cwd, PATH..." (also legacy-payload section 2). Missing: invoke Node entry directly rather than spawn fgos recursively, parent forwards termination, Unix signal equivalence and Windows process-tree as explicit target-specific tests (compatibility-harness lists only "target-specific signal/process-tree behavior").
Section heading content (payload identity, ownership, repair) is carried by the Legacy Payload contract; its title is the closest heading.

Target states the identity and unmoved file; the explicit "three things separated" framing (public name, payload identity, file location) is not stated in the contract (public name after R1 is in spec.md section 3 only).

Target carries payload identity legacy-node and unmoved file; the public-name row (fgos to Rust host, workspace shim) lives only in spec.md, and the "components.legacyNode and legacy_payload field of every legacy-cli descriptor" binding is only partly stated; Today column absent.

Target carries unmoved/unrenamed, payload = package.json files incl. bin/fgos.mjs and bin/fgos-runner.mjs, staged whole under components.legacyNode.root. Missing: decision date 2026-09-10, rationale (package root from file location, relative ../src imports, Repo Layout Vision section 7, src/state and src/runner mislabel), libexec/legacy-node, zero import changes, rename only when payload deleted.

Target carries the join(...) resolution and the ban on PATH, caller cwd, hardcoded path, alternate bin entry. Missing: dev:<rev> declaring root ".", entry bin/fgos.mjs, entries.fgos target/release/fgos; staged release root libexec/legacy-node, entries.fgos bin/fgos; "one mechanism for dogfood and production".

package.json bin.fgos is removed or pointed at the workspace shim when Rust host becomes default; bin.fgos-runner stays until runner migrates; header in bin/fgos.mjs and root AGENTS.md state the ownership rule. Targets only note (roadmap.md line 38) that bin.fgos still points at bin/fgos.mjs and (legacy-payload alignment) that fgos-runner remains the public Node entry; the removal plan and the ownership header/AGENTS.md rule are absent.

Target says Node payload tests may spawn bin/fgos.mjs directly and production call sites use a single resolver preferring workspace shim tier 0. Missing: ~150 grep hits vs ~9 real call sites and their list, the three Herdr sites, per-runtime resolver (bin-discovery.mjs, shell function, resolve_fgos), fallback to node bin/fgos.mjs without fgctl init, ~75 tests stay, comments are not callers.
Target: every selector has exactly one generated CommandRouteDescriptor. Missing: derived from the Node command registry plus checked migration annotations.
All six minimum fields (selector, route_kind, operation_id, legacy_payload, owner_path, compatibility_tests) appear in the target field table with the same rules.

Target: descriptor may not name both routes active; unlisted selector fails the build. Missing: legacy-cli means Node owns parsing and Rust only recognizes the checked selector and preserves OsString argv (partly in spec.md section 5 and legacy transition), native means typed provider owns the operation with legacy kept only as a bounded rollback oracle.

Target says scripts/explain-command-route.mjs "should read the same artifact" and metadata is drift-validated. Missing: that it prints route kind, owner path, payload identity and compatibility suites, and the CI rejections (missing owner/proof, registry-descriptor drift enforced, direct production spawn outside LegacyCliPassthroughProvider, payload removal before binding removal).

Target (vision table, also release-boundaries and history): rollback of native R1/R2 behavior is release rollback through fgctl, not a provider-selection toggle; config cannot replace built-in providers (history). Missing: previous release still ships both native provider and Node payload during observation window, and the explicit "none is promised anywhere in this stack".
Section 3 (command metadata and parser ownership) is carried by the descriptor rules and spec section 5; heading closest to command-route-descriptor Rules.

Metadata separation: host-visible identity/summary/namespace/provider mapping; host-owned projection from CLI/REST/MCP input to an operation request; provider-owned semantic validation; transitional provider-owned CLI parsing for legacy-cli selectors; router need not parse every host grammar. host-use-cases.md only lists host responsibilities generally; no target states this four-way split.

Target spec section 5: recognize only checked selector, preserve OsString, no provider-owned flag parsing, no legacy.<verb> OperationId. Missing: "reserved CLI-only compatibility contract" and that when a command becomes native its option grammar and typed request conversion move together to avoid two parsers.
Target rule: generated metadata is validated for drift and is not a second hand-maintained source of truth; same meaning.
Section 4 (presentation versus semantic outcome) is carried by the preserved rules on fgos.v1 and stdout/stderr presentation.
Target alignment row "fgos.v1 belongs to CLI presenter" plus invocation-kernel (ProviderOutcome is not fgos.v1, HTTP, MCP) and r3 proof (remote does not emit fgos.v1) carry this.
Target preserved rules: legacy CLI output is not wrapped in a second fgos.v1 envelope; captured stdout/stderr remain public presentation; invocation-kernel adds ProviderOutcome is not fgos.v1.

fgos.v1 hashes compact JSON.stringify(data) bytes but prints a two-space pretty envelope; cross-runtime tests separate semantic data equality, compact hash input, hash output, envelope order/pretty rendering, timestamp shape, trailing newline, stdout/stderr, exit/signal mapping. Compatibility-harness only requires byte capture of stdout/stderr and exit/signal; none of the hash/pretty separation is stated.

Golden vectors are necessary but not sufficient; a Node-generated differential corpus (object order, integer limits, negative zero, float exponent, Unicode/control, nested, null/bool), timestamps checked by shape, no byte parity inferred from the narrow version payload. No target mentions differential corpus or these cases.
Section "Rust Host First" is carried by node-to-rust-migration Selected Direction (Rust host first, Node legacy payload until each boundary is ready).

Target vision section 3 says Rust becomes host first because it establishes the permanent composition root and plugin seam while Node stays available. Missing: peer host use cases and provider registry placed in the permanent runtime, and "every native migration removes a LegacyNode edge instead of building infrastructure into a temporary Node host".

Cost of Rust-host-first: a legacy CLI call pays Rust launcher plus Node startup, distribution ships both runtimes, compatibility failures may precede any speedup, and the payoff requires the first Rust host to stay thin and forward legacy behavior. No target states these costs or the thin-host condition.
Related Documents heading corresponds to the target Related Files section.

Target Related Files lists descriptor, payload, harness and source docs only. Missing links to the kernel contract (host-invocation-provider-routing), External Provider Protocol, and Runtime Identity And Activation with its note that it owns the payload on-disk location, fgctl rollback mechanics and the init/doctor tail superseding legacy setup onboarding.
